metaData.originalTitle: Best practices for computer and browser use with Claude | Claude
metaData.title: Best practices for computer and browser use with Claude | Claude
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides official best practices for integrating Claude's computer and browser use capabilities, focusing on screenshot scaling, resolution selection, click accuracy optimization, thinking effort tuning, and prompt injection defense.
metaData.summary: This blog post from the official Claude blog offers a comprehensive guide for developers building computer use agents with Claude's latest models (4.6 family and Opus 4.7). It identifies the single highest-impact optimization as pre-downscaling screenshots to fit API limits (1568px long edge / 1.15MP for 4.6; 2576px / 3.75MP for Opus 4.7) to prevent silent downscaling and coordinate mismatch. Recommended starting resolutions are 1280x720 for 4.6 models and 1080p for Opus 4.7, with a provided Python function for 'max API fit' per-image scaling. The guide covers diagnosing click issues (consistently offset, near misses, wrong element), model selection (Sonnet 4.6 for mechanical precision, Opus 4.7 for reasoning), handling small targets via zoom and keyboard alternatives, and content ordering (text before image). It also presents detailed recommendations for adaptive thinking effort levels: 'medium' is the sweet spot for 4.6 models, while 'high' is the default for Opus 4.7. Finally, it discusses prompt injection defenses, including training-time robustness, real-time classifiers, and continuous red teaming.
metaData.featuredReason: Anthropic engineers lay out the full operational playbook from running Computer Use and Browser Use internally. The foundational fix: pre-downscale screenshots to match Claude 4.6 (1568px / 1.15MP) or Opus 4.7 (2576px / 3.75MP) limits — otherwise the model picks coordinates on a degraded image and the whole agent loop collapses. The piece covers effort-level tuning, prompt injection defense, a three-pronged context discipline (cache breakpoints, scrolling buffer, LLM compression), plus experimental batch tools and advisor patterns. A genuine production checklist.

mainPoints.point: Pre-downscaling screenshots to fit API limits is the single most impactful optimization for click accuracy.
mainPoints.explanation: Screenshots exceeding the API's internal processing limits (1568px/1.15MP for 4.6, 2576px/3.75MP for Opus 4.7) are silently downscaled, causing a mismatch between the model's perceived image and the coordinate space, leading to consistently offset clicks.

mainPoints.point: For Claude 4.6 models, 'medium' thinking effort provides the best accuracy-to-cost ratio, while 'high' is the recommended default for Opus 4.7.
mainPoints.explanation: UI automation tasks are primarily perceptual, not deeply logical. Medium effort achieves near-maximum success rates at half the token cost of high for 4.6 models. For Opus 4.7, high effort is the default for complex multi-step interactions.

mainPoints.point: Place text instructions before the image in the messages content array to improve click accuracy.
mainPoints.explanation: This ordering lets the model know what to look for as it processes the screenshot, which improves the accuracy of its click predictions compared to placing the image first.

mainPoints.point: Prompt injection is a serious risk for computer use agents, requiring multi-layered defenses.
mainPoints.explanation: Agents interact with untrusted content by design. Anthropic's defense strategy includes training-time robustness via reinforcement learning, real-time classifiers that scan for adversarial content, and continuous red teaming.

keyQuotes: Click accuracy is the foundation of any computer use integration. If clicks don't land where they should, nothing downstream works: forms don't get filled, buttons don't get pressed, and workflows fail.
The single highest impact optimization is also one of the simplest: pre downscale your screenshots before sending them to the API.
Setting effort to medium achieves close to the highest task success rate while using roughly half the output tokens of high.

UI automation tasks are fundamentally different from coding or math problems. Most computer use actions are perceptual and mechanical: identifying the right element, clicking in the right place, rather than deeply logical.
